_meta.description: GPU catalog for the VRAM/throughput planner — capacity, bandwidth, dense BF16 compute, and 3-tier hourly pricing. Keyed by slug (t4-16, a100-80, ...), the same convention benchmarks/data.json's GPU half of each key uses. index.html's GPU_TABLE and generate_report.py's GPUS are generated from this file by tools/sync_data.py, between 'GPU_TABLE:BEGIN'/'GPU_TABLE:END' marker comments in each — edit this file, then re-run that script; do not hand-edit the generated blocks. The row schema is deliberately narrow: only the fields every engine already reads today. It is designed to grow — a vendor tag, a per-board device count, a fabric/interconnect tier are all expected to land on this same table in later commits — so a new column is the likely shape of that change, not a new table.

schema.gb: VRAM per card, in GiB. Matches the manufacturer's marketing number, which is already GiB in practice — nvidia-smi reports an '80 GB' H100 as 79.6 GiB, not 80/1e9*2^30 worth of decimal GB.
schema.bw: Memory bandwidth in GB/s, used as the decode roofline's bandwidth term.
schema.hyper: Hyperscaler on-demand price in $/hr per GPU (AWS/GCP/Azure).
schema.spec: Specialized-cloud price in $/hr per GPU (Lambda, CoreWeave, RunPod and similar).
schema.spot: Spot/marketplace price in $/hr per GPU (Vast.ai and similar).
schema.tflops: Dense BF16 tensor-core TFLOPS. NVIDIA datasheets headline the 2:4-structured-sparsity number (e.g. H100 SXM '1,979 teraFLOPS* / *With sparsity'); LLM inference does not use structured sparsity, so this is the dense figure — half the headline number.
schema.name: Display name shown in the GPU dropdown's option label and in generate_report.py's PDF/CLI output, e.g. 'H100 80 GB'.
